question: Should OpenClaw adopt tools.exec.denylist as the canonical config-owned STOP policy that overrides ordinary full/off and durable trust while preserving authorized elevated-full as the explicit break-glass bypass?
rationale: Source review can assess implementation consistency, but only maintainers can authorize this permanent operator-facing security precedence and decide whether the policy belongs in openclaw.json rather than the host approvals store.

options.title: Approve the documented contract
options.body: Accept config-owned deny-over-allow semantics and the elevated-full exception, then require clean current-head integrated companion proof before merge.

options.title: Require host-owned policy
options.body: Rework the feature so the authoritative STOP rules live with host approvals, with an explicit compatibility and management design.

options.title: Decline the core feature
options.body: Keep the existing deny, allowlist, and full modes and close both implementation candidates without adding a new policy surface.

recommendation.title: Approve the documented contract
recommendation.body: Accept config-owned deny-over-allow semantics and the elevated-full exception, then require clean current-head integrated companion proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history and PR discussion most strongly connect this person to the exec approval and break-glass security contract.
